_about: Bomber hit rates on ships by kind (release 2; the design director's rulings of 22 November 2026 18:13Z and 18:27Z on the historian's counts, /mnt/project-files/historian/bomber-hit-rates-ships-1122.md; the form at air-battles/hitrates/form-hit-rates-by-kind.md). src/campaign/hitrates.ts. With the switch on, a strike on ships no longer counts the law's single 0.04 a bomber times its crews' naval skill, nor the spoil, nor the harbour's x1.5 and a surprise's x3: each bomber that released is worth its kind's rate for its navy, by whether fighters were over the ships ('covered') or not ('open'). 'underWay' holds each navy's own counted rows; a navy without a row takes its senior partner's ('kin'), then 'pool' (the rows pooled across the navies counted, D). 'anchor': ships at anchor, the rows that were the surprises (Taranto 0.55 and Pearl 0.72 a torpedo, their middle 0.64; Pearl's armour-piercing bombs 0.175, D); a dive bomber at anchor is its row under way times 'diveTimes' (today's harbour factor, a knob). 'fixed': the month (turn) from which a navy's own row gives way to the pool (America's torpedoes once the Mk 13's faults were cured, turn 61; see '_fixed'). 'types', 'landShares' and 'landKinds': a land bomber group's kind, by its type where the game carries one, else by the record's count, else by the historian's kinds by nation (see '_land'). 'mast': mast-height attacks (Bismarck Sea, wartime claims, L), only where the field has that attack: it has none today. 'on' is the switch for a new grand campaign; it cannot ship on until 'sourced' (the land kinds, M today, and the rows the design director has open).
_pool: D, from the historian's rows, per bomber that released. Dive, open: Japan's alone (Cornwall 8 of 16, Sims 3 of 4) = 0.55. Dive, covered: Japan 3 of 33, America 11.5 of 76 (Midway's carrier SBDs 8.5 of 48, Shokaku 3 of 28), Germany about 6 of 30 (Illustrious) = 20.5 of 139 = 0.15. Torpedo (the design director's 18:40Z and 18:45Z; America's 1942 drops left out, a weapon's fault, not its crews): open, every counted case with no fighters over the ships: Force Z 10-11 of 61 (the wrecks, USSBS) and the Nells at Crace's cruisers 0 of 12 = 10.5 of 73 = 0.14, Japan's row and the pool; covered, the Kates at Coral Sea alone, 2 of 13 = 0.15. Britain's torpedo under way: 0.14 both rows, the middle of 0.13-0.15 (Swordfish at Bismarck, the historian's 6.1). Level (18:52Z, every Japanese case in Japan's own row, as for torpedoes): Japan open, Force Z (2-3 hits from 27 level bombers, the middle 2.5) and Crace's cruisers (about 18, 0 hits) = 2.5 of 45 = 0.06; Japan has no covered case and takes the pool's 0 (D); America 0 (Midway's B-17s and Coral Sea, from high up); the pool, the counted cases with a bomber count: 0.06 open, and Midway's afternoon B-17s, 0 of 12 = 0 covered. Mast height: 0.5 a bomb (Bismarck Sea, L).
_fixed: America's torpedo is 0 until the Mk 13 was fixed and issued: from turn 61 (the design director's 18:40Z), the middle of fixed by midsummer 1944 (59) and widely issued by autumn 1944 (62), the historian's 6.4 (L); the pool from then.
_land: A land bomber group's kind (the design director's 18:40Z: shares by year NOT FOUND; a type names its kind by definition; where the game carries no type, the historian's kinds by nation, M, until sourced; no share of ours). 'types': the game's land bomber types (battle/air/doctrine.ts bomberOf: the B-17, He 111 and Lancaster, all level, ruling 59; the Stuka dives). 'landShares': a nation's split by kind only where the record counts one, by [from turn, {kind: share}]: Japan's navy at Force Z, 61 torpedo and 27 level planes of 88 (USSBS, the Genzan commander's own table, F; the historian's 6.2). 'landKinds': the historian's kinds by nation and year (6.3, from memory, M), by [from turn, [kinds]], for a plain type ('Bomber:ITA'); a group whose nation lists several kinds and no share counts equal shares of them, the middle of the possible mixes (D, the design director's 18:45Z), until shares are sourced. Turns: autumn 1940 = 14, 1942 = 29, 1943 = 41, Aug 1943 = 48, 1944 = 53, Mar 1943 = 43.
_takes: Hits to sink each class with the switch on (the design director's 19:48Z on the historian's case count, air-battles/hitrates/historian-hits-to-sink-1122.md): each hit counts one; hits per ship sunk, overkill left out. Battleship under way 6.25 (Repulse and Prince of Wales); at anchor 8 (the design director's 20:00Z on CINCPAC's Pearl report, F: 36 hits over 4.5 sunk, Nevada half; was 7); the Yamato class 25.5 (the middle of 20 and 31) once the class rows can tell her, till then 6.25 like every battleship ('yamato', not read yet); carrier 5.7 (Shoho and Hermes out); cruiser 8 (Mikuma and Mogami; Cornwall, Dorsetshire and Yahagi out); destroyer 2.25. Submarines are not aimed at (carriers.json strike.aim 0); their row is the old one. The old takes (carriers.json strike.takes) retire with the switch on.
_kindTakes: The kind form (the design director's 19:53Z and 19:54Z on the historian's case count; air-battles/hitrates/form-aim-and-kind-1122.md): with the switch on, the law keeps a strike's hits in two jugs, bombs (dive, level and mast height) and torpedoes, shares each over the classes by the aim, and a ship sinks when her bombs over her class's bomb take and her torpedoes over its torpedo take add up to one. These replace 'takes' and 'takesAnchor' above (the all-kind takes of 19:48Z, kept as the reference). Pure cases only, overkill out, survivors in (D). Battleship under way: torpedoes 5.25 (Repulse 5 and Prince of Wales 5.5, their one bomb each set aside); bombs null: no battleship at sea was sunk or hit to sinking by bombs alone, so bombs hit her but do not sink her until a case is counted. At anchor (20:07Z: every count the middle of its sources, no mixing): bombs 10 (Arizona 5, the middle of 2 and CINCPAC's about eight, sunk; Tennessee 2, Maryland 2, Pennsylvania 1 lived: 10 over 1), torpedoes 6 (Oklahoma's middle; Utah out, an old target ship). Carrier: bombs 6.5 (Akagi, Kaga, Soryu, Hiryu sunk; Shokaku twice, Yorktown, Enterprise twice lived: 26 over 4); torpedoes 4.33 (19:54Z and 20:00Z: every carrier torpedo case pooled with the bombs' share taken out at 6.5: Taiho 1, Shokaku 3.5, Lexington 3.5, Hornet 3, Yorktown 4 in the end = 15 over 5 sunk less 10/6.5, Hornet's 5 bombs with the crashes left out). Cruiser: bombs 8 (Mikuma 3 sunk, Mogami 5 lived); torpedoes 9 (the design director's 20:29Z on the historian's 20:42Z: Canberra 1 and Houston 2 lived, Chicago 2 and then 4 the next afternoon, sunk: 9 over 1; Chikuma out, her some 200 shells a kind the air law does not hold and her end disputed). Bombs on a battleship at sea stay not laid: Roma's two Fritz X were a guided armour-piercing bomb, a kind of its own the game's aircraft do not carry (the after-release list). Destroyer: bombs 3 (Sims 3 sunk, and Ten-Go's Suzutsuki 1 lived and Kasumi 2 scuttled, counted sunk as the scuttled carriers are: 6 over 2; the design director's 20:33Z); torpedoes 6 over 4 (Hammann 1, Barton 2, Jarvis 2, and Ten-Go's Hamakaze 1; Isokaze and Asashimo out until counted). Submarines are not aimed at; their row is the old one. The tests before code (Yorktown on 4 June 0.92, afloat; Lexington 1.12 and Hornet 1.46, sunk; the five carriers 5 of 5; Taiho 0.23 and Shokaku 0.81 short, fuel vapour and damage control the field does not know; Pearl's eight battleships 4.73 against 4.5 on the middles, California 0.57 short, a reading: her open hatches, not her count) are in tests/hit-rates-by-kind.test.ts.
_armedAboard: Strike on deck (the design director's 20:25Z on air-battles/hitrates/form-spill-and-deck-1122.md and the historian's marks): a carrier is ARMED ABOARD while her fleet's strike wing is aboard, fit to fly and has not flown this month, or has flown this month against a land target and is back aboard rearming (carriers.ts deckOf); she is OFF once the wing has flown against ships this month, while it rests or is unfit, and with no strike wing aboard. Armed aboard, bombs 3.25 (the design director's 20:33Z): Akagi 1, Kaga 4, Soryu 3 and Princeton 1, all sunk, and Franklin 2 and Bunker Hill 2, both lived (the historian's 20:42Z and 20:58Z; Bunker Hill's two crashes named, not counted: the law holds no crash kind), 13 over 4. Hiryu joins only when marked; late-war damage control, a candidate cause the record does not separate, is not laid. Off, bombs: a GAP (bounded below by the survivors and above by Hermes), so the carrier bomb take above stands in, and the switch stays off while the gap stands. Torpedoes: the carrier take above for both states until the bombs' row is laid. At anchor the same state. Shown, never counted, beyond this row.
_aim: Where a strike's hits land, by class (the aim form; the design director's 19:53Z, form 1's picks, and 19:59Z on the historian's strike count, air-battles/hitrates/historian-hits-by-class-per-strike-1122.md). Pooled (D): all hits on a class over the counted strikes, over all the ships of that class present in them, set so the battleship's is 1; no weight of ours, small counts as found. The strikes at sea that found carriers or battleships, as the design director read them (rows 1 and 3-12; Pearl, the one strike at anchor, and Hermes, where Vampire's 16 hits fell beside a carrier already finished, are out; row 13's ships present are from memory and are out; a screen not counted on the page is left out of its class's sum): carriers 69.5 hits over 22 present, battleships 13.5 over 10, cruisers 5 over 25, destroyers 0 over 62. So carrier 2.34, battleship 1, cruiser 0.148, destroyer 0. A class the counted strikes never hit takes 0 while a class with aim above 0 is present; a strike that finds only such classes shares its hits by ship count. Submarines stay unaimed (0). A row with fewer than three counted strikes is not laid and the other row stands for it (20:07Z): at anchor there is one (Pearl), so this row stands there; the historian is asked for Taranto, Tungsten and Kure toward an anchor row. One aim for both kinds for now: the historian's bomb and torpedo columns stay apart in the count for a kind aim later. The old weights (carriers.json strike.aim: battleship 2, carrier 3, cruiser 1, destroyer 0.5, ours) retire with the switch on.
